## Problem and intended outcome

Explain the concrete problem and the behavior this change should produce. Link the canonical work specification or existing task authority.

## Change and scope

Describe the meaningful implementation/design choices and affected interfaces. Identify preserved behavior for an existing system. Link decisions rather than duplicating them.

## Verification

Record actual checks, candidate identity, results, and evidence links. State required checks that could not run and their practical effect. Distinguish local, CI, native-client, and cloud observations. Identify review scope and whether it was independent when relevant.

## Delivery and recovery

Describe applicable release identity, configuration, operational effects, and recovery. Mark nonapplicable fields with a reason; retain the project's actual required checks and release controls. Do not imply deployment or approval merely from PR creation.

## Continuation

Link the current tasks/handoff and identify any remaining blocker or next action. Avoid a competing task checklist in this PR description.
